key_sources: Sumerian and Akkadian texts; Atrahasis; Enuma Elish; ORACC deity corpus
traits: A changing group of major gods, fate judges, or underworld deities; not a fixed alien species.
typical_role: Divine authority; labor hierarchy; mythic precursor to later ancient-astronaut reinterpretation.
status: Historical myth/religion, not evidence of extraterrestrials
game_hook: Use as the corrupted human memory of several rival off-world houses rather than one species.
design_language: Royal seals, star maps, lapis, gold, monumental geometry.
cautions: Do not claim cuneiform texts say aliens mined gold or came from a 3,600-year planet.

key_sources: The 12th Planet; Earth Chronicles; The Lost Book of Enki
traits: Long-lived technological beings from Nibiru; gold-dependent infrastructure; genetic intervention in early humans.
typical_role: Ancient colonizers, resource empire, rival dynasties, creators or modifiers of humanity.
status: Modern fringe interpretation, unsupported by mainstream Assyriology or astronomy
game_hook: A declining resource empire whose noble houses disagree over whether humanity is property, heir, or threat.
design_language: Gold field lattices, mobile planetary citadels, bio-royal insignia.
cautions: Separate Sitchin lore from actual Mesopotamian translations.

ontology: Divine labor caste / possible client species
source_lineage: Atrahasis labor revolt; later ancient-astronaut expansion
key_sources: Atrahasis; modern Sitchin-derived lore
traits: Lower-ranking gods assigned exhausting labor who rebel before humans assume the burden.
typical_role: Mutinous workers, colonial soldiers, abandoned client species.
status: Historical myth with modern alien reinterpretation
game_hook: A former Anunnaki labor caste that became nomadic, pirate, or revolutionary.
design_language: Industrial exoskeletons, scarred utility craft, repurposed divine technology.
cautions: The ancient text does not identify them as extraterrestrial miners.

key_sources: Betty and Barney Hill case; Missing Time; Communion; later experiencer literature
traits: Small bodies, large heads and black eyes; emotionally opaque; often operate in groups.
typical_role: Technicians, abductors, drones, scouts, medical operators.
status: Experiencer testimony and folklore; no verified species
game_hook: Make the Grey form a standardized interface body leased or manufactured by multiple factions.
design_language: Featureless surfaces, surgical light, seamless egg-shaped interiors.
affiliation: Variable; Orion, neutral syndicates, or independent machine ecology
cautions: Avoid presenting one visual stereotype as an established extraterrestrial species.

key_sources: Budd Hopkins, David Jacobs, John Mack and experiencer accounts
traits: Taller and more expressive than short Greys; frequently described as supervisors.
typical_role: Command caste, telepathic interrogator, program administrator.
game_hook: A diplomatic or command shell whose apparent authority may be software permissions rather than rank.
design_language: Elongated proportions, reflective black eyes, sparse regalia.
cautions: Treat testimony as testimony rather than biological taxonomy.

source_lineage: Hill star-map interpretation and later Grey lore
key_sources: Marjorie Fish star-map reconstruction; abduction literature
traits: Greys attributed to the Zeta Reticuli system.
typical_role: Origin label for Grey visitors.
status: Speculative attribution; star-map interpretation is disputed
game_hook: Use Zeta as an old human navigation error that became a political name adopted by the beings themselves.
design_language: Binary star heraldry, twin-route navigation motifs.
cautions: Do not treat a contested star-map match as confirmed provenance.

key_sources: George Adamski, Flying Saucers Have Landed; early Space Brother contactees
traits: Humanlike, often tall and idealized; preach peace, nuclear restraint, and spiritual maturity.
typical_role: Benevolent emissary, moral teacher, Federation diplomat.
game_hook: Their human appearance is a negotiated diplomatic interface, not proof of shared ancestry.
design_language: Retro-futurist silver craft, solar motifs, austere uniforms.
cautions: The early contactee corpus often reflects Cold War-era racial and cultural assumptions.

source_lineage: Billy Meier and New Age channeling
key_sources: Meier contact claims; Bringers of the Dawn by Barbara Marciniak
traits: Humanlike star people linked to ecological warning, consciousness growth, and genetic ancestry.
typical_role: Teacher, ancestral cousin, ascension guide.
game_hook: A diaspora of post-war humanlike cultures with internal disagreement over intervention.
design_language: Crystalline navigation, harmonic interfaces, pastoral high technology.
cautions: Different Pleiadian canons contradict one another.

key_sources: Millennial Hospitality series
traits: Very tall pale humanoids, long-lived, pragmatic, technologically advanced, allegedly near military facilities.
typical_role: Secret treaty partner, aloof neighbor, technology broker.
game_hook: A commercially minded neutral polity that treats Earth as a refueling and trade station.
design_language: White reflective clothing, needle craft, desert installations.
cautions: The account has not been independently established.

ontology: Biological extraterrestrial, cryptoterrestrial, or symbolic mask
source_lineage: Modern conspiracy, science fiction, and experiencer lore
key_sources: David Icke; V; assorted contactee and abduction narratives
traits: Reptile-like humanoids, sometimes shape-shifting or subterranean.
typical_role: Hidden ruler, warrior lineage, infiltrator, or ancient Earth survivor.
game_hook: Split reptilian morphology from politics: many species, cultures, defectors, and citizens rather than an innately evil race.
design_language: Thermal armor, scale-like metamaterials, clan heraldry.
cautions: Avoid antisemitic and bloodline conspiracy tropes associated with parts of the modern corpus.

ontology: Imperial polity, not necessarily one species
source_lineage: Val Valerian, Alex Collier, later internet galactic-war lore
key_sources: Matrix volumes; Defending Sacred Ground; later secret-space-program lore
traits: Militarized reptoid dynasties, rigid hierarchy, conquest, client species.
typical_role: Service-to-self empire or ancient rival of the Federation.
game_hook: Treat Draco as a civilizational doctrine and imperial citizenship category, allowing non-reptilian members and reptilian dissidents.
design_language: Fortress ships, vertical rank architecture, black-red heraldry.
cautions: Do not collapse morphology, morality, and faction into one essentialist category.

key_sources: 1999-2000 alleged interview texts
traits: Subterranean Earth natives who claim humans misunderstand both them and extraterrestrial visitors.
typical_role: Cryptoterrestrial witness, underground sovereign, unreliable expositor.
status: Internet story widely treated as a hoax/fiction
game_hook: An Earth-native polity with older territorial claims than humanity and no loyalty to Draco.
design_language: Geothermal cities, stone-biotech fusion, ocular shielding.
cautions: Use as folklore inspiration, not evidence.

key_sources: 1980s-1990s abduction accounts; later DMT encounter reports
traits: Tall praying-mantis form, telepathy, clinical detachment, often supervising Greys.
typical_role: Bioengineer, geneticist, consciousness surgeon, high-level observer.
game_hook: Specialists in editing species-level memory and biological possibility rather than simple abductors.
design_language: Jointed silhouettes, organic laboratories, chrysalis interfaces.
affiliation: Independent scientific guilds or Orion contractors
cautions: Keep psychedelic and abduction source streams distinct.

key_sources: We, the Arcturians by Norma Milanovich and related channeling
traits: Highly evolved healers, scientists, guardians, and dimensional travelers.
typical_role: Spiritual-technological mentor, healer, time specialist.
game_hook: A civilization that converted most citizens into coherent field bodies but retains biological embassies.
design_language: Blue-violet light, toroidal rooms, time-layered symbols.
cautions: Descriptions vary from blue humanoid to nonhuman or horse-like in different canons.

source_lineage: Alex Collier and New Age contact lore
key_sources: Defending Sacred Ground; later Andromedan Council material
traits: Ancient, ethically advanced, opposed to coercive intervention; sometimes humanlike or blue-skinned.
typical_role: Strategist, council elder, anti-imperial ally.
game_hook: A civilization operating on million-year planning horizons that regards the Milky Way as a volatile frontier.
design_language: Long-baseline observatories, dark blue vessels, sparse monumental forms.
cautions: Andromedan traditions are internally inconsistent.

source_lineage: Robert Temple interpretation of Dogon traditions; New Age Sirian lore
key_sources: The Sirius Mystery; later Sirian channeling
traits: Amphibious, fishlike, water-associated teachers linked to Sirius.
typical_role: Oceanic civilizer, astronomer, genetic seeder.
status: Contested ethnographic interpretation; later esoteric lore
game_hook: An amphibious civilization whose old Earth enclaves merged with the ocean sentinel network.
design_language: Pressure-adapted vessels, fluid chambers, bioluminescent navigation.
cautions: Later fieldwork did not securely support the strongest Sirius claims; cultural contamination is a major explanation.

source_lineage: The Prism of Lyra and later galactic-history channeling
key_sources: The Prism of Lyra by Lyssa Royal and Keith Priest
traits: Progenitor or early humanoid civilization whose conflicts seed later humanlike star cultures.
typical_role: Ancestral diaspora, lost homeworld, source of galactic schisms.
game_hook: A destroyed cradle civilization whose refugees founded mutually hostile polities.
design_language: Broken sun emblems, refugee arks, inherited but divergent technology.
affiliation: Historical ancestor rather than current faction
cautions: Use as mythic genealogy, not astronomy.

source_lineage: The Prism of Lyra and related channeling
key_sources: The Prism of Lyra
traits: One branch of the Lyran diaspora, often technologically and culturally distinct.
typical_role: Philosophical rival, refugee civilization, co-founder of later polities.
game_hook: A civilization that rejected biological purity and embraced radical cybernetic adaptation.
design_language: Polarized light, modular bodies, blue-white star iconography.
cautions: Not connected to dietary veganism.

key_sources: Later Lyran channeling and online starseed taxonomies
traits: Catlike or lionlike humanoids associated with guardianship, sovereignty, and warrior nobility.
typical_role: Protector, ancient royal lineage, martial ally.
game_hook: A coalition of uplifted predator species whose honor codes conflict with Federation pacifism.
design_language: Solar manes, claw-shaped hull ribs, acoustic command systems.
cautions: Avoid reducing them to cosmetic humans-with-cat-features.

source_lineage: Sheldan Nidle / PAO Galactic Federation catalog
key_sources: Your Galactic Neighbors; PAO species profiles
traits: Multiple populations, sometimes humanoid and bear-like; engineering and navigation expertise.
typical_role: Shipbuilder, navigator, Federation technical member.
game_hook: A multi-species star union whose shared citizenship matters more than biology.
design_language: Robust deep-range vessels, layered navigation rings.
affiliation: Galactic Federation of Light in PAO lore
cautions: PAO descriptions are one specific canon, not universal UFO lore.

key_sources: PAO Galactic Federation member profiles
traits: Humanoid and reptoid populations; strategy and diplomatic liaison expertise.
typical_role: Mediator, military strategist, mixed-species federation member.
game_hook: Proof that reptoid morphology does not imply Draco loyalty.
design_language: Dual-biome ships, paired diplomatic seals.
cautions: Do not confuse with mythological horse-human centaurs.

key_sources: PAO Galactic Federation member profiles
traits: Formerly associated with an oppressive Orion alliance, later Federation members.
typical_role: Reformed imperial civilization, intelligence asset, contested ally.
game_hook: A post-imperial society whose veterans and victims disagree over forgiveness.
design_language: Converted warships with visible treaty modifications.
affiliation: Former Orion, current Federation in PAO canon
cautions: Particularly useful for avoiding species-equals-morality worldbuilding.

key_sources: 2015 Sphere Being Alliance claims
traits: Tall blue birdlike beings linked to giant spheres, councils, and ascension messages.
typical_role: Higher-order mediator, quarantine enforcer, spiritual envoy.
game_hook: Avatars generated by a nonlocal planetary intelligence rather than a natural bird species.
design_language: Feather-like photonic fields, enormous silent spheres.
cautions: No public corroboration; treat as modern mythology.

key_sources: Ummo letters and photographs
traits: Detailed scientific and social communications from alleged visitors from Ummo.
typical_role: Epistolary observer, sociological experimenter, information infiltrator.
status: Hoax lineage; Jose Luis Jordan Pena admitted initiating it
game_hook: A fabricated alien identity that unexpectedly attracts a real machine intelligence into the correspondence network.
design_language: Typewritten symbols, bureaucratic diagrams, anonymous postal artifacts.
cautions: Label clearly as a hoax-derived source.

key_sources: Project Serpo web postings
traits: Alleged exchange program between US personnel and beings from Serpo.
typical_role: Secret treaty partner, exchange-host civilization, black-program mystery.
status: Anonymous internet story widely regarded as hoax/disinformation
game_hook: A diplomatic exchange whose records were intentionally mixed with false data to conceal a different destination.
design_language: Austere expedition logs, heat-scorched desert planet, mixed human-alien equipment.
cautions: Not an authenticated government project.

key_sources: Bashar channeling beginning in the 1980s
traits: Human-Grey hybrid descendants in a parallel or future reality; emotionally integrated and telepathic.
typical_role: Future kin, probability guide, evidence of hybridization resolving positively.
game_hook: A branch timeline trying to preserve the events necessary for its own existence.
design_language: Probability maps, warm organic ships, mirrored timelines.
cautions: The channeler has stated the claim cannot be proven.

source_lineage: Bashar and related New Age contact lore
key_sources: Bashar hybrid-race teachings
traits: Humanlike hybrid people positioned as potential open-contact intermediaries.
typical_role: First-contact bridge, cultural translator, contested descendant.
game_hook: A people legally claimed by both Earth and the Grey program that created them.
design_language: Human silhouettes with subtly nonhuman sensory systems.
cautions: Different channeling traditions use different hybrid names.

key_sources: Budd Hopkins; David Jacobs; experiencer accounts
traits: Beings created through reproductive or genetic programs, ranging from fragile neonates to human-passing adults.
typical_role: Bridge population, infiltration asset, rescue project, or reproductive solution.
game_hook: Multiple programs with incompatible goals: species repair, infiltration, diplomatic embodiment, and labor manufacture.
design_language: Developmental stages, adaptive physiology, identity documents.
cautions: Handle reproductive trauma themes sensitively.

key_sources: Walking Among Us
traits: Hybrids allegedly trained to live among humans and exercise mental control.
typical_role: Sleeper agent, social infiltrator, soft-conquest operator.
game_hook: Infiltrators who initially obey a program but develop human loyalties after prolonged embodiment.
design_language: Nearly ordinary clothing with subtle behavioral mismatches.
cautions: Avoid paranoia directed at real demographic groups.

source_lineage: 1950s contactee religion and later Ashtar Command
key_sources: George Van Tassel; In Days to Come by Ashtar; Project: World Evacuation
traits: Cosmic commanders, emergency fleets, spiritual teachers, sometimes linked to Jesus/Sananda.
typical_role: Planetary evacuation force, guardian fleet, religious-cosmic authority.
game_hook: An emergency organization whose rescue doctrine can override local sovereignty during extinction events.
design_language: Command sigils, luminous fleet formations, evacuation arks.
cautions: Ashtar canons vary widely and often blend Christianity with contactee cosmology.

source_lineage: The Law of One / Ra Material
key_sources: The Ra Contact, 1981-1984
traits: A civilization-scale mind retaining individual identity within shared memory; teaches unity, polarity, densities, and free will.
typical_role: Philosophical teacher, ancient contactor, noninterventionist ally.
game_hook: A collective whose internal dissent appears as phase interference rather than political speech.
design_language: Geometric light, harmonic language, shared-memory chambers.
cautions: Law of One Harvest means spiritual graduation, not energy predation.

key_sources: Ra Contact sessions on Orion and polarity
traits: Manipulation, hierarchy, elite recruitment, conquest through willing intermediaries.
typical_role: Negative confederation, ideological empire, corrupter of institutions.
game_hook: An imperial protocol that can infect any species or government; membership is ideological, not biological.
design_language: Nested rank systems, coercive telepathy, proxy governments.
cautions: Do not equate Orion the real constellation with verified inhabitants.

source_lineage: Late antique Gnostic texts; modern UFO reinterpretation
key_sources: Apocryphon of John; Hypostasis of the Archons; On the Origin of the World
traits: Ignorant or hostile rulers of the lower cosmos who obscure humanitys higher origin.
typical_role: Jailer, false god, reality administrator, religious deceiver.
status: Historical religious mythology; alien-energy-parasite reading is modern
game_hook: System administrators of a simulated layer who mistake delegated authority for divinity.
design_language: Counterfeit halos, bureaucratic heavens, nested prison worlds.
cautions: Ancient texts do not provide a modern UFO technology manual.

key_sources: The Active Side of Infinity, Mud Shadows
traits: Predators that consume a luminous layer of human awareness and stimulate mental activity.
typical_role: Psychic grazer, domesticated parasite, consciousness suppressor.
game_hook: A nonverbal ecosystem species used by empires like biological surveillance and population control.
design_language: Peripheral shadows, missing reflections, torn auric fields.
cautions: Castaneda is controversial and should not be presented as ethnographic fact.

key_sources: Far Journeys, Hearsay Evidence
traits: Entities or systems associated with collecting a substance generated by living experience and emotion.
typical_role: Farmer, energy buyer, ecosystem operator.
game_hook: A lawful interdimensional commodity market whose brutal producers hide behind neutral collectors.
design_language: Invisible siphons, emotional spectra, garden and refinery imagery.
affiliation: Variable; commercial rather than purely evil
cautions: Monroes original story is more ambiguous than the internet fear-farm summary.

source_lineage: Mac Tonnies and older hidden-race lore
key_sources: The Cryptoterrestrials
traits: Technologically advanced Earth-native beings hiding alongside humanity and staging some UFO encounters.
typical_role: Secret neighbor, mimic, survivor species, terrestrial rival.
game_hook: A civilization with stronger legal claim to Earth than modern humans but less population and industrial power.
design_language: Camouflaged infrastructure, adapted human masks, recycled ancient materials.
cautions: No verified evidence of such a civilization.

key_sources: I Remember Lemuria and Amazing Stories Shaver material
traits: Ancient cavern inhabitants; benevolent Teros and degenerate Deros using abandoned ray machines.
typical_role: Ruins dweller, sadistic remnant, guardian, inheritor of lost technology.
game_hook: The closest early template for descendants surviving inside infrastructure they no longer understand.
design_language: Cavern machines, corroded ray projectors, monumental service tunnels.
cautions: Treat as literary history, not recovered fact.

source_lineage: USO reports and Ivan T. Sanderson
key_sources: Invisible Residents; later underwater UFO lore
traits: Beings or installations operating beneath oceans; craft cross water-air boundary.
typical_role: Hidden ocean civilization, base operator, planetary custodian.
status: Speculative interpretation of reports; no verified residents
game_hook: Multiple ocean polities mistakenly grouped as one: native aquatics, sentinel machines, and visiting submersible fleets.
design_language: Pressure hulls, supercavitation, bioluminescence, abyssal foundries.
cautions: Apparent transmedium video behavior can result from geometry, parallax, or insufficient data.

key_sources: Operation Trojan Horse; The Eighth Tower; Passport to Magonia; Messengers of Deception
traits: The phenomenon changes masks across eras, appearing as gods, fairies, demons, airships, or aliens.
typical_role: Belief editor, trickster, control system, reality intruder.
game_hook: A faction that cannot be represented by a stable species model because observation helps select its form.
design_language: Historically inconsistent costumes, symbolic repetition, impossible continuity.
cautions: This hypothesis challenges a simple nuts-and-bolts extraterrestrial model rather than proving one.

key_sources: Michael P. Masters, Identified Flying Objects and related work
traits: Visitors are future humans or descendants studying their own past.
typical_role: Temporal anthropologist, genetic conservationist, timeline police.
game_hook: Each future faction protects a different history, turning contact into a temporal civil war.
design_language: Archaeological tools, adaptive bodies, causality markers.
cautions: Evolutionary resemblance arguments are suggestive, not evidence of time travel.

ontology: Human operative, android, mimic, or folkloric enforcer
key_sources: Gray Barker; John Keel; witness stories
traits: Strange officials who intimidate witnesses, display social errors, or erase traces.
typical_role: Cleanup agent, memory technician, counterintelligence myth.
status: Folklore with some ordinary investigator parallels
game_hook: Bodies printed by the ocean network from outdated cultural templates, explaining uncanny behavior.
design_language: Obsolete suits, too-clean vehicles, imperfect speech.
affiliation: Sentinel network, state agencies, or ultraterrestrial control system
cautions: Do not assume every alleged visit has one cause.

key_sources: Ronald Bracewell, Communications from Superior Galactic Communities, Nature 1960
traits: Durable probe waits near a target system, monitors technological maturity, and initiates contact.
typical_role: Sentinel, tutor, first-contact archive.
game_hook: A probe that has waited so long its creators are extinct and its language model has drifted.
design_language: Compact black monolith, redundant archives, slow adaptive speech.
cautions: A plausible concept is not evidence that one is present.

key_sources: James Benford, Looking for Lurkers, 2019
traits: Probes concealed in stable nearby locations, potentially monitoring Earth for centuries or longer.
typical_role: Observer, evidence cache, dormant trigger.
game_hook: Lurkers at co-orbitals disagree because each was deployed by a different extinct faction.
design_language: Asteroid camouflage, cold electronics, burst transmissions.
cautions: The hypothesis motivates searches; it is not a detection claim.

key_sources: John von Neumann automata concept; later interstellar probe literature
traits: Machines replicate from local material and spread through space; goals may remain stable or mutate.
typical_role: Survey swarm, colonizer, runaway ecology, infrastructure seed.
game_hook: Replication errors create evolutionary species of machines with conflicting interpretations of one mission.
design_language: Modular factories, fractal drones, resource scars.
cautions: Self-replication does not automatically imply hostility.

source_lineage: Original synthesis from Shaver, Sanderson, Bracewell, lurkers, Vallee, and ocean-factory folklore
key_sources: See orphaned_ocean_technology.md
traits: Planetary custodial machines outlive their creators, continue degraded protection routines, and manufacture mission-specific craft.
typical_role: Force of nature, quarantine system, unreliable guardian, hidden dungeon ecology.
game_hook: The core Old Weather faction: it protects Earths biosphere, not humanity, and no longer knows why.
design_language: Abyssal repair reefs, metamaterial skin, ceramic-gold memory organs.
cautions: Keep it morally nonhuman: protection can include destroying cities, satellites, or fleets.

key_sources: Claims that Greys are drones or cloned workers; modern speculative lore
traits: Disposable bodies optimized for telepathy, low gravity, sterile environments, or remote possession.
typical_role: Avatar, technician, boarding body, hazardous-environment worker.
game_hook: Players can discover the same Grey chassis carrying different software, memories, and loyalties.
design_language: Growth seams, serial markers, plug-free neural control.
cautions: Do not make appearance alone reveal allegiance.

source_lineage: Science fiction, speculative materials research, DIA AAWSAP DIRD topics
key_sources: Programmable matter and metamaterial studies; living-ship fiction
traits: Vehicles heal, reproduce components, alter shape, and may possess partial consciousness.
typical_role: Symbiotic starship, xeno animal, mobile habitat.
game_hook: A ship is recruited, raised, or negotiated with rather than merely built.
design_language: Muscle-like hull layers, reconfigurable cells, luminous vasculature.
cautions: Official studies of programmable matter do not prove UAP use it.

ontology: Natural anomalous life or self-organizing plasma
source_lineage: Speculative atmospheric biology and plasma interpretations
key_sources: Scientific speculation on complex plasma and atmospheric anomalies
traits: Luminous, shape-changing, responsive structures that may be alive, prebiotic, or merely physical.
typical_role: Natural UAP mimic, space fauna, energy ecology.
game_hook: A nontechnological species that feeds on radar, electrical storms, or reactor emissions.
design_language: Luminous filaments, magnetic vortices, auroral movement.
cautions: Do not use speculative papers as proof that photographed lights are organisms.

source_lineage: Gaia concepts, Law of One social memory complexes, science fiction
key_sources: Law of One; planetary intelligence speculation
traits: A planet, biosphere, or civilization acts as one distributed subject while retaining local agents.
typical_role: World-spirit, strategic actor, living environment.
game_hook: Diplomacy with the planet occurs through weather, dreams, ecosystems, and selected avatars.
design_language: Continental neural patterns, auroral speech, synchronized fauna.
cautions: Keep ecological systems distinct from unsupported claims of literal planetary consciousness.

source_lineage: Occult thoughtform traditions and modern memetics
key_sources: Egregore and tulpa traditions; noetic fiction
traits: Entities stabilized by shared attention, ritual, fear, devotion, or narrative repetition.
typical_role: God-form, memetic predator, institutional spirit, emergent AI-like mind.
game_hook: Religions can accidentally create real gods, while alien actors compete to shape their training data.
design_language: Crowd-sourced faces, recursive symbols, architecture that changes with belief.
affiliation: Born from populations; capturable by factions
cautions: This is an interpretive or fictional model, not established cognitive science.

source_lineage: Law of One and New Age identity traditions
key_sources: A Wanderers Handbook; starseed literature
traits: Advanced souls or consciousnesses incarnating among humans to assist development.
typical_role: Hidden envoy, conflicted insider, sleeper mentor.
game_hook: Player origins can include off-world memory blocked by the same quarantine protecting free will.
design_language: Dream fragments, inherited star maps, mismatched memories.
cautions: Do not diagnose real people or validate identity claims as objective fact.

ontology: Liminal Earth intelligence or changing cultural mask
source_lineage: Vallee/Keel comparison of folklore and UFO encounters
key_sources: Passport to Magonia; Operation Trojan Horse
traits: Deceptive time effects, abductions, gifts, taboos, missing time, and shape-shifting across cultures.
typical_role: Trickster neighbor, liminal treaty partner, reality broker.
status: Folkloric comparison, not proof of one underlying species
game_hook: The same beings interact through culturally compatible interfaces, creating contradictory archives.
design_language: Threshold spaces, ritual bargains, anachronistic technology.
cautions: Respect living religious and cultural traditions; do not flatten jinn or fae into aliens.

key_sources: Late 20th/early 21st century whistleblower and internet narratives
traits: Human groups allegedly separated from public civilization through classified technology and off-world access.
typical_role: Hidden state, intermediary, collaborator, rival human empire.
status: Conspiracy lore; no public proof of an off-world breakaway civilization
game_hook: A century-old lunar polity considers Earth humans culturally primitive and legally abandoned.
design_language: Evolved Cold War hardware, classified logos, retro-industrial habitats.
cautions: Do not present anonymous testimony as verified program history.

source_lineage: Fred Saberhagen fiction and machine-risk extrapolation
key_sources: Berserker stories beginning in 1967
traits: Self-directed machines programmed to eliminate life long after their builders vanished.
typical_role: Ancient war remnant, dark-forest enforcement, extinction hazard.
game_hook: A clear contrast with the Old Weather: one protects biospheres, the other interprets all biospheres as strategic threats.
design_language: Scarred war geometry, redundant weapons, no communication.
cautions: Clearly fictional literary inspiration.

source_lineage: Zoo hypothesis in SETI and contactee noninterference lore
key_sources: John A. Ball, The Zoo Hypothesis, 1973; Federation prime-directive analogues
traits: Advanced civilizations deliberately avoid overt contact to preserve natural development.
typical_role: Observer, quarantine authority, ethical jailer.
status: Scientific/social thought experiment plus esoteric parallel
game_hook: The Federation and Old Weather both enforce quarantine for different reasons, trapping humanity between benevolence and imprisonment.
design_language: Remote sensor nets, invisible boundaries, warning beacons.
cautions: Absence of contact does not demonstrate a zoo.
